name: Aurach bei Kitzbühel
kurzbeschreibung: Peaceful village along the Jochbergstraße, featuring stunning hiking trails into the Kitzbüheler Alpen and a charming, traditional village center.
beschreibung:
Overview

Aurach bei Kitzbühel is a picturesque Tyrolean village in the Kitzbühel district, situated at an altitude of around 846 meters in the Leukental along the Auracher Ache stream. Located just five kilometers south of the world-famous alpine sports resort of Kitzbühel, the municipality counts approximately 1,200 inhabitants and extends up to alpine peaks such as Mount Gebra at 2,057 meters and Großer Bischof at 2,127 meters. Serving as a peaceful, rural counterpart to glamorous Kitzbühel, Aurach charms visitors with rolling alpine meadows, centuries-old heritage farmhouses adorned with vibrant flowers, and living traditions. Awarded the European Hiking Seal of Quality alongside Jochberg, it provides superb year-round recreation.

History

Settlement around Aurach dates back to prehistoric times, as copper ore was extracted on the slopes of the Kelchalpe and Gebra as early as the Bronze Age. The village was first documented around 1250 as Owirowe and in 1280 as Auraw. The name stems from Old High German, referring to a river meadow grazed by the aurochs. Copper mining flourished from the 16th to the 18th century before finally ceasing in 1926; the historic miners' accommodation on the Kelchalm operates today as the Bochumer Hütte mountain lodge. The district of Kitzbühel including Aurach became part of Tyrol in 1506 under Emperor Maximilian I. The village is famously recognized by its Gothic parish church of Saint Rupert with its slender Baroque onion dome erected in 1664, which served as a renowned motif in the paintings of Alfons Walde. The 500-year-old Hallerwirt inn and the Branderhof have frequently hosted film and television productions.

How to Get There

Motorists reach Aurach via the Inntal motorway A12, exiting at Wörgl-Ost or Kufstein-Süd and following the federal highway B178 via St. Johann in Tirol, then continuing along the Pass-Thurn-Straße B161 through Kitzbühel to Aurach. From Salzburg and the Pinzgau region, the B161 crosses via Mittersill and the Pass Thurn pass. By train, long-distance Railjet and Eurocity trains arrive at Kitzbühel Hauptbahnhof. From the railway station, regular regional bus route 4010 connects to Aurach in less than ten minutes. Free winter ski buses connect directly to adjacent ski lifts.

Tips

The top attraction is the Aurach Wildlife Park at 1,100 meters on the sunny slopes of the Branderhof, representing the largest open-air animal enclosure in Tyrol with over 350 animals including red deer, alpine ibex, mouflons, yaks, and lynx, featuring a petting zoo for children. Hikers can embark on scenic tours to the Bochumer Hütte, Hochwildalm, and Mount Gebra. A visit to the historic Hallerwirt inn treats guests to authentic stone pine dining parlors and traditional Tyrolean cuisine. In winter, skiers enjoy direct proximity to the world-renowned KitzSki area via the Wagstättbahn in Jochberg or Kitzbühel's cable cars, while the scenic Leukental cross-country ski trail delights Nordic enthusiasts.
